title: ENH: number field arithmetic in the GUI
body:
Adds functionality to the SpinBoxes in the GUI by which their values can be modified using simple mathematical expressions (Python syntax).

# Checklist: `x` (done) or `~` (irrelevant)

- [x] [I am familiar with **ASE's contribution guidelines.**](https://ase-lib.org/development/contribute.html)
- [ ] [**Doc strings** in code changed in this MR are up to date.](https://ase-lib.org/development/python_codingstandard.html#writing-documentation-in-the-code)
- [x] [**Unit tests** have been added for new or changed code.](https://ase-lib.org/development/tests.html)
- [x] [**Changes** have been added in `changelog.d` using `scriv`.](https://ase-lib.org/development/writing_changelog.html)
author: lempelto

comments.author: yuzie007
comments.body:
Presently the arithmetic is valid only for magnitudes, not for elements of lattice vectors and angles.

The arithmetic feature can be generally applicable to any spinboxes that accept numbers.
So, it would be very best if we can put the parsing logic not for individual boxes but somewhere upstream. Please see my other comments for details.

comments.author: lempelto
comments.body:
Thank you very much for the comments, @yuzie007

At least in my testing, the feature does already work for all spinboxes including vectors and angles but only if you press Enter in the SpinBox (the `ui.SpinBox.parse_and_callback` wrapper does the evaluation). At first (in 3e795023829ebd045cd3e05ea5dfbb6cbac918e3), I did have the evaluation in the 'value' property but then the math was only resolved when the value was read and I specifically liked being able to always see the result by pressing Enter, even when Enter wasn't bound to another event. But I'm realizing now that we should be able to have the best of both worlds and add `self.parse_value()` to the 'value' getter and it'll work more robustly, so I will change that.

comments.author: yuzie007
comments.body:
Thank you @lempelto for your quick response!

I also realized that your original implementation worked as well when I press Enter for in the Spinbox. The issue I wrote existed the "Apply Vectors" and the "Apply Angles" buttons apart from "Apply Magnitudes".

Thank you so much for your revision. May I ask you to check one more thing here? As far as I tested on my environment (Apple Silicon MacOS), the revision of `value` is sufficient, and `parse_and_callback` may be not necessary, because `value` will be called from the original `callback` in e.g. `apply_magnitudes` in `celleditor.py`.

The other thing is about the potential security risk of `eval`; please have a look on
- https://leapcell.io/blog/python-eval-how-it-works-and-why-its-risky, particularly "Security Vulnerabilities"
- https://stackoverflow.com/a/34904657

After a survey, I found ASE already has a nice and safe `eval_expression` in `ase.utils.parsemath`. With this, we probably do not need `parse_input_arithmetic` and can simply do
```python
from ase.utils.parsemath import eval_expression
...
    @property
    def value(self):
        return eval_expression(self.widget.get().replace(',', '.'))
```
This allows us to give even `sqrt(2.0)`. Would you also think it's reasonable?

comments.author: lempelto
comments.body:
Hi. I just pushed some changes and I'll mention the rest here.

> As far as I tested on my environment (Apple Silicon MacOS), the revision of `value` is sufficient, and `parse_and_callback` may be not necessary, because `value` will be called from the original `callback` in e.g. `apply_magnitudes` in `celleditor.py`

This is true, but the `parse_and_callback` will also work even when no callback has been set (e.g. the SpinBoxes in the 'Add atoms' dialog don't have callbacks). It's not strictly necessary but this way you can still press Enter to evaluate the entered expression, which I like. Thus I would prefer keeping the wrappers. It also neatly makes it so that we don't get `TypeError: 'NoneType' object is not callable` messages.

> The other thing is about the potential security risk of `eval`

I was aware of this but figured that anyone using ASE probably has access to a Python interpreter to run their malicious code in. A simple check was in place to make sure no text (e.g. functions with names) would be evaluated.

Regardless, the `ase.utils.parsemath.eval_expression` function is certainly the better option and I've now changed the code to use it instead. I probably would have used it to begin with had I realized it existed :grin:

comments.author: yuzie007
comments.body:

I now fully agree on the present version.

```

    return self.func(*args)

  File "/Users/ikeda/codes/ase/ase/gui/ui.py", line 235, in <lambda>

                                          ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
```

The present MR also addresses this with `parse_and_callback`.

comments.author: yuzie007
yuzie007
comments.body:
Thank you @lempelto for the MR!
I like this arithmetic feature very much.
This will largely strengthen the GUI functionality.

Presently the arithmetic feature is available only for magnitudes, but this feature can probably be enabled for all spinboxes.
With a quick test, I found, maybe we can just update the `value` property of `ase.gui.ui.SpinBox`.
If you agree, could you implement this?

Having the test is very nice.
I believe we can merge this MR soon.

comments.author: yuzie007
comments.body:
For my own notes; we need to consider two cases:

1. Hitting Enter in the `Spinbox`. Then the code should once parse the expression given in the box, and, if necessary, reflect the given change via `callback`. (This is done now with `parse_and_callback`).
2. Clicking buttons like "Apply Magnitudes"  in the cell editor, which reflect given changes in (possibly) multiple `Spinbox`es simultaneously. In mamy cases, these buttons refer to the `value` attributes of the `Spinbox`es directly. So, the parsing is needed also at this timing.

To make these well explicit, it is nice to call `parse_value` both in `parse_and_callback` and in the `value` attribute, as exactly implemeneted in the present MR.

@askhl: The present MR looks to me a very good enhancement. If no comments further, I would like to merge in a few days.

comments.author: yuzie007
comments.body: Thank you @lempelto once again for the MR! I would like to merge now.
